What it pays for

The card works on real hardware today. The gap between a working prototype and a card people can trust is a list of specific jobs, each with a price. Donations go to the first unfunded item on this list, in order.

JobWhy it comes firstStatus
Independent security review of the applet, NUT-CCP, and the host toolsNo one outside the project has reviewed the design yet. The first review will change it, so it comes before cards reach more hands.Unfunded
Silicon tests: tear-off, timing, and skimming rangeThese attacks are untested on real chips. They need lab time, a few dozen cards, and someone whose job is to break them.Unfunded
Printed card runs for pilotsBlank cards cost $6 to $12 each in small lots. A run of 500 printed cards puts the card in the hands that will find the next problem.Unfunded
Field pilots with community mintsTills, cards, and operator support for the first communities that issue cards on their own mint.Unfunded
Development timeThe protocol, applet, apps, and ops service are maintained by people who need to eat. A month of funded time is a month of fixes shipped.Unfunded

Costs are posted here as quotes come in. When an item is funded, its row says so and the receipts appear in Where it went.

How to send

Donations are received by Island Bitcoin LLC, which runs cashucard.org, ops.cashucard.org, and the Provisioner app. They are gifts toward the work on this page, with no goods, services, or equity in return, and they are not tax deductible.

Pick an amount and scan the code with any Lightning wallet.

Grants and larger gifts

Foundations and companies that want to fund a whole line item, such as the security review, can write to hello@cashucard.org. We will send a one-page scope with the deliverable, the reviewer or vendor, the timeline, and what gets published at the end. Reviews and test reports funded this way are published in full in the repository.

The work so far was carried by grants from The Reynolds Foundation and the Human Rights Foundation under Project Island Resilience, and by Flash and Island Bitcoin.

Other ways to help

  • Break it. Audit the applet and host code or the draft NUT, and report what you find to security@cashucard.org.
  • Build on it. Add card support to your wallet or till. The developer page has the protocol, the simulator, and the test vectors.
  • Issue cards. Run cards on your own mint with the install guide and an operator account on ops.cashucard.org, load small amounts, and tell us what fails.
  • Talk about it. Questions and ideas go in GitHub Discussions.
